feature: The timing strip reads a Forever spinner's turn
summary: Pick a layer with a Forever motion and the strip's header says how long one turn takes ("800 ms per turn") and whether the turn ends where it starts. With only a spinner moving, the strip is called One turn and has no lap to type, as on the spinner mock.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Walks: a-lone-spinner-strip-reads-one-turn-walk and forever-spinner-keeps-its-own-pace-walk.

try.do: Draw an ellipse, pick it, and choose Add Motion > Rotation in the panel.
Set From to 0, To to 360, Curve to Linear, Repeat to Forever and Over to 800.
Read the strip's header: ONE TURN, 800 ms per turn, and a green ends where it starts.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Draw a rectangle and give it the Rotation Add Motion offers (a 900 ms swing), then pick the ellipse again.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Type 300 into To and read the header: an orange does not end where it starts.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Type 360 back into To and watch the header go green again.

evaluate: Does "800 ms per turn" beside the lap make it clear which number is the spinner's speed?
Is the orange "does not end where it starts" the warning you want for a turn that jumps, or too loud?
With a swing beside the spinner, the header still says ONE CYCLE and shows the 900 ms lap. Is that the right title there, or should it name the turn too?
With the spinner alone, does losing the lap field feel right, or do you miss being able to type a lap?
rough: Side by side with icon-loop-wt.html step 5 ("Put it back, and look at the join"): the header matches the mock's dock bar, ONE TURN, a loop mark with 800 ms per turn, then a green check with ends where it starts.
No mock covers a turn that does not join, which this task's checklist asked to be said: the app reads "does not end where it starts" in orange with a warning mark, the mock's own words turned round.
No mock covers a spinner beside a swing: there the app keeps the ONE CYCLE title and its lap field, since the swing still shares the lap, and adds the turn reading after it.
The ruler's 800 tick and the repeats label are drawn on top of each other when the lap ends on a tick (picture 2); filed as the-repeats-label-on-the-timing-strip-s-ruler-ne.
The turn reading shows only for the picked layer, and for its first Forever motion when it has several; another layer's spinner is not read until it is picked.
